finding.spoofability.partial: The domain is only partly protected against spoofing (score {score}/100, risk {risk})
finding.spoofability.spoofable: The domain is easily spoofed (score {score}/100, risk {risk})
finding.spoofability.subdomains: Subdomains can be spoofed: the DMARC subdomain policy is weaker than the domain policy
module.spoofability.checks: Computes, from SPF and DMARC, a 0 to 100 score of how easily the domain can be spoofed, a risk level, a verdict and attack scenarios, subdomains included.
module.spoofability.fix:
Open the module detail (score, risk level, attack scenarios) to see what weighs on the result: SPF missing, open or ending in `~all`, DMARC missing or at `p=none`, partial enforcement (`pct=`), weaker subdomain protection (`sp=`).
SPF: publish a single TXT record at the domain apex, ending in `-all`, with no `+all` and no `include` that allows any sender (see the Email security module).
DMARC: publish `_dmarc.example.com` with `p=none` and a `rua` address, read the reports for 2 to 4 weeks, then move to `p=quarantine` and finally to `p=reject` once every legitimate sender is compliant.
Remove any `pct=` value below 100: otherwise part of the forged messages escapes the policy.
Subdomains: align `sp=` with `p=` (for example `sp=reject`) or remove `sp=` so they inherit `p`, and check that no subdomain publishes its own weaker `_dmarc`.
Do not rely on DKIM alone or on a spam filter: they do not stop an attacker from showing your address as the sender. Only an enforced DMARC (with aligned SPF or DKIM) makes receivers reject or quarantine forged messages.
Check with `dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com`, then run the scan again: the spoofing score should go down.
module.spoofability.fix_snippet:
# DNS SPF
example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=spf1 include:_spf.example.net -all"
# DNS DMARC p=reject
_dmarc.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=reject; sp=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com"
# dig
dig +short TXT example.com
dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com
module.spoofability.title: Spoofing risk
module.spoofability.why: Successful spoofing lets attackers send fake messages in the domain's name (CEO fraud, phishing) that land in your customers' inboxes.
spoofability.dmarc_monitor: DMARC in monitoring mode (p=none): nothing is blocked
spoofability.dmarc_partial: DMARC enforced on only {pct}% of messages
spoofability.dmarc_quarantine: DMARC quarantine: fake messages go to spam
spoofability.dmarc_reject: DMARC reject: fake messages are rejected
spoofability.no_dmarc_data: DMARC could not be read: spoofing score impossible
spoofability.no_email_data: E-mail analysis result unavailable: spoofing score impossible
spoofability.scenario_from: Anyone can send a message showing an @{domain} address: without enforced DMARC, nothing forces the receiver to reject it
spoofability.scenario_partial: With pct={pct}, part of the fake messages escapes the DMARC policy
spoofability.scenario_spf_open: An SPF that authorises any sender lets an attacker pass DMARC through SPF alignment
spoofability.scenario_subdomains: Subdomains are less protected (sp={policy}): an attacker can spoof one
spoofability.spf_open: SPF authorises any sender (+all or open include)
